threads.body: The existing shared callback tests expect a client span, so they do not protect these `context == null` branches. Add regression tests for suppressed completion and failure/cancellation before initialization in both this module and the 5.0 `WrappedFutureCallback` (lines 189–228). Verify captured custom context values, including without a caller span, and restoration of an unrelated callback-thread context after normal and throwing delegate exits.

replies.body: Added regression tests for both clients in 3a3dca92a2. The integration tests cover suppressed completion with a custom context value and no caller or client span. The wrapper tests verify that early failure and cancellation run with the captured caller context and restore the previous context on both normal and throwing exits. All six tests fail without the fix and pass with it.

threads.body: This suite pins `httpclient5:5.0`, so `-PtestLatestDeps=true` still runs these wrapper tests against the baseline instead of the latest supported client version; the matching fixed dependency also appears at `instrumentation/apache-httpasyncclient-4.1/javaagent/build.gradle.kts:25`. Select both suite dependencies with `baseVersion(...).orLatest()` so the custom suites honor latest-dependency mode.

replies.body: Keeping the baseline versions here. The wrapper tests mock `FutureCallback` and check our context scoping; they don't exercise version-specific Apache client behavior. The installed-agent integration tests already exercise real requests in latest-dependency mode. We’re documenting the distinction in #21464.
Simplified `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled` in both versions in e45fc92a498. Each method now opens one caller-context scope for the delegate, after logging or ending the span.
